Subject: SilverPlate production capacity profile

Hi Kimberly / Ben,

Quick context: we're getting closer to GA for SilverPlate (customer-facing search + summarization). We need Redwood to size a Dedicated pool we can commit to for Q3. High-level workload below — happy to share more traces if useful (attached an excerpt of our SLA doc).

Traffic profile (expected):
- Steady baseline: ~1,800 tokens/sec sustained (aggregated across endpoints)
- Typical day peaks: 6k tokens/sec for 3–5 minute bursts (several times/day)
- Rare extreme spikes: up to ~12k tokens/sec for <30s during marketing events

Performance target / SLO: 95th latency <= 250ms for the primary endpoint (model: Llama2-70B-quantized variant; responses average 600 tokens). We need a plan that keeps us within that P95 at committed throughput, and an explicit fallback/hedge for spikes.

Can you model tokens/sec -> GPU footprint and give a committed tier + burst policy recommendation? Also please call out the headroom percentage you recommend and any alternative model variants (smaller quantized) if we want lower committed spend.

Thanks — Elliot
Elliot Hayes

Subject: Re: SilverPlate — footprint & headroom estimate (workbook attached)

Kim / Ben,

I took the Novum numbers and ran a conservative mapping. Assumptions up front:
- Model: Llama2-70B q4_K_M-like quantization (weights on GPU, KV cache in GPU when possible).
- Avg response length 600 tokens, median request length 40 tokens.
- Measured sustained per-H100(80GB) steady-state throughput for this model ~700 tokens/sec (single request mix with streaming disabled); peak single-node burst absorbency up to ~1,800 tokens/sec for short intervals with warmed KV.

Sizing summary (committed + burst):
- Committed pool recommendation: 6x H100-80GB nodes (private/dedicated). Rationale: 6 nodes -> committed sustained capacity ~4,200 tokens/sec (6 * 700). This covers baseline (1,800) and leaves ~2,400 tokens/sec headroom for day-to-day growth and variability.
- Burst absorption (short spikes): with autoscaling/burst policy we can provision up to +50% additional nodes on demand (soft burst to 9 nodes) to absorb typical peaks (~6k). With warm cache and request shaping, we can hit ~6,300 tokens/sec for 2–5 minute bursts.
- Extreme spikes (12k tokens/sec): recommend a two-pronged strategy — (A) rapid fallback routing to Llama2-30B-quant variant (approx per-node sustained 1,300 tps) and (B) request-level throttling/queueing for non-critical queries. Using an L2-30B fallback adds effective burst capacity without immediate hardware scale (6 H100 + L2-30B instances -> combined soft-capacity ~9k tokens/sec).

Headroom guidance: aim for 30–40% operational headroom above committed sustained to ensure SLO stability (we've observed tail latency growth when headroom <25%). With 6 nodes, Novum would have ~35% headroom relative to peak-of-day expectations (6k). For P95 <= 250ms we should also:
- Enable prefix caching for common prompts (can cut tokens served by 8–12% on this workload)
- Use request-level timeouts and prioritized queues for low-latency endpoints

Cost/ops notes: 6x H100 committed with a burst policy to 9 nodes is operationally simple and predictable for billing. If Novum opts for lower cost, committing 4 H100 could be discussed but we'd see tighter headroom (~10–15%) and higher SLO risk during bursts.

Attachments: capacity_workbook.xlsx (contains per-node throughput curves, latency-by-load plots, and a fallback latency delta matrix).

If helpful I can produce a variant table showing exact P95 delta for 6 vs 4 nodes and for L2-70B vs L2-30B fallback; want that before I send a formal proposal?

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: SilverPlate capacity proposal & burst contingency (DEAL-8792)

Hi Elliot — thanks again for the profile and patience while we modeled this. Attached is a concise proposal (PDF) but summary below.

Proposal (high level):
- Committed capacity: 6x H100-80GB dedicated nodes (Redwood Dedicated) — covers baseline + day-to-day headroom.
- Burst policy: soft autoscale to +3 nodes (total 9) for 2–10 minute bursts; policy triggers on queue depth and 90th percentile CPU/GPU saturation.
- Fallback: automatic routing to Llama2-30B-quantized variant when sustained incoming tokens/sec exceed 9k; expected P95 delta ~+40–80ms depending on prompt length but keeps SLA intact during event spikes.
- Headroom: ~35% operational headroom vs expected peak-of-day (6k). We recommend an SLA acceptance test during canary (30–72 hours) with traffic replay to validate p95.

Commercials & next steps:
- We attached a one-page pricing snapshot and the technical workbook (so you can see the per-node numbers). Contracting / DocuSign link is provided below — if you want edits to burst terms or a longer canary window we can iterate.
- Next step: approve commercial term and select desired fallback policy (auto-fallback to 30B vs manual toggle).
